request.query: The customer changed clause 9 (Limitation of Liability): “Neither party will” → “Customer will not”. We sent: "to the claim. Neither party will be liable for indirect". They returned: "to the claim. Customer will not be liable for indirect". How should the deal desk respond?

documents.title: Payment terms: standard position
documents.text: Our standard is net thirty days from the invoice date. Do not volunteer anything longer.

documents.title: Payment terms: deals under $100,000 a year
documents.text: For subscriptions under $100,000 in annual fees, the deal desk may agree to net forty-five days without further approval.

documents.title: Payment terms: deals of $100,000 a year or more
documents.text: For subscriptions of $100,000 or more in annual fees, the deal desk may agree to net forty-five days. Net sixty days needs the approval of the VP Finance. Anything longer than sixty days is refused.

documents.title: Fees: the fee in the agreement must match the signed order form
documents.text: The annual fee in the agreement must equal the fee on the signed order form. Any other figure is treated as an error or an attempted discount and goes back to the account executive. The deal desk cannot approve a discount.

documents.title: Fees: renewal price increases
documents.text: Our standard renewal increase cap is 5%. The deal desk may lower the cap to 3% for an initial term of three years or longer. A cap below 3%, or a price freeze, needs the approval of the VP Finance.

documents.title: Fees: late payment interest
documents.text: Late payment interest of 1.5% per month is standard. The deal desk may accept 1% per month. Below 1% needs the approval of the VP Finance.

documents.title: Term: length of the initial term
documents.text: Pricing on the order form depends on the length of the initial term. A shorter initial term than the one quoted needs a new quote from the account executive. The deal desk cannot shorten the initial term.

documents.title: Term: notice of non-renewal
documents.text: We ask for sixty days' notice of non-renewal. The deal desk may accept thirty days. Shorter than thirty days needs the approval of the VP Customer Success because it leaves no time to plan capacity.

documents.title: Term: termination for convenience
documents.text: We do not give customers a right to terminate for convenience. If the customer insists, escalate to Legal. Legal may offer termination for convenience after the first twelve months with no refund of prepaid fees.

documents.title: Liability: the cap
documents.text: Our liability cap is the fees paid in the twelve months before the claim. The deal desk may not change the cap. Legal may agree to twenty-four months of fees for deals of $150,000 or more in annual fees. Anything above twenty-four months is refused.

documents.title: Liability: excluded damages
documents.text: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages is not negotiable by the deal desk. Any edit to it goes to Legal.

documents.title: Service levels: availability commitment
documents.text: We commit to 99.9% monthly availability. A higher commitment such as 99.95% or 99.99% is only available on the Enterprise Plus plan and needs the approval of the VP Engineering.

documents.title: Service levels: service credits
documents.text: Service credits are capped at 10% of the monthly fee and are the sole remedy. The deal desk may raise the cap to 15%. Credits must always have a maximum: a minimum credit, or no cap, is refused.

documents.title: Governing law: standard position
documents.text: Delaware law and Wilmington courts are standard. The deal desk may accept New York law and courts without approval.

documents.title: Governing law: any other state
documents.text: Any governing law or venue other than Delaware or New York, including the customer's home state, needs the approval of Legal before signature.

documents.title: Data: export window after termination
documents.text: We keep customer data available for export for thirty days after termination. The deal desk may extend this to ninety days. Longer retention has a storage cost and needs the approval of the VP Engineering.

documents.title: Confidentiality: how long it lasts
documents.text: Confidentiality obligations last three years after termination. The deal desk may accept up to five years. Longer periods, or perpetual confidentiality, go to Legal.

documents.title: Assignment: consent
documents.text: Assignment needs the other party's consent except in a merger or sale of the business. The deal desk may allow the customer to assign to an affiliate that is not a competitor. One-sided assignment rights go to Legal.

documents.title: Notices: address changes
documents.text: A change to the customer's notice address is administrative. Accept it and update the account record.

request.instructions: The passages are internal playbook rules for the Provider's deal desk. A passage answers the query only if it tells the deal desk how to respond to this specific change for a deal of this size.
